name: Helmo Rénovation
description: A 2-month redesign of a renovation company's WordPress site: SEO, UI and UX for its 64 pages, with an assistant I trained. The 83 blog articles of the 147-page site weren't my work.
context: Helmo Rénovation is a French all-trades renovation company (interiors, energy retrofits, professional projects) working turnkey with its own teams. The site runs on WordPress and Elementor, hosted by Hostinger.

work.title: Team and my role
work.text: Two of us: me and an assistant I trained along the way.
points: I directed the work and often built model pages for the assistant to copy.
I split the tasks; by the end we each owned a set of pages, so site-wide changes no longer needed sharing out.
The assistant did simple no-code edits; I handled global CSS, caching and the CEO's new requests.

work.title: Site architecture
work.text: A broad offer sorted into clear topic silos.
points: Three silos: interior renovation, energy renovation, services for professionals.
Sub-pages by property type, room and trade (insulation, heating, ventilation, electrical, plumbing…).
Internal links within each silo, breadcrumbs everywhere.

work.title: SEO for the 64 site pages
work.text: One search intent per page, each optimised on its own.
points: Unique titles and meta descriptions written to earn the click.
One H1 per page, a clean H2/H3 hierarchy.
A segmented XML sitemap (pages, posts, categories).

work.title: Images, markup and speed
work.text: Readable by machines, fast on mobile.
points: Every image renamed, with alt text based on what it shows and the page's keyword, for search engines and screen readers.
schema.org markup: Organization and LocalBusiness, WebSite and WebPage on every page, BreadcrumbList.
LiteSpeed cache (built into Hostinger), WebP images lazy-loaded off screen, unused Elementor elements and scripts removed.

work.title: FAQ rewritten for GEO
work.text: So ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity can quote it.
points: Questions worded the way a customer asks an AI.
The answer first, details after, in short factual sentences.

design.summary: On the interface side: a night blue that builds trust, an orange reserved for calls to action, and a single typeface, Poppins, for fast reading on mobile.
